device.name: Dexterous Gym EggHandOver-v0 (two fixed Shadow hands, egg handover)

facts.text: EggHandOver-v0 is registered with entry point dexterous_gym.envs.egg_hand_over:EggHandOver, max_episode_steps 75 and reward_type 'dense'
The EggHandOver model file is dexterous_gym/envs/hand/egg_handover.xml
EggHandOver constructs TwoHandsEnv with moving_hands False, two_objects False and target_rotation 'xyz'
TwoHandsEnv has 40 actions when moving_hands is False and 52 when it is True
The action space is Box(-1.0, 1.0, shape=(n_actions,), dtype float32)
Each action component is mapped to the actuator control range as centre + action*range and clipped to the range
step clips the action, applies it, advances the simulator and returns (observation, reward, done, info) with done hard-coded False
The observation dictionary carries observation, achieved_goal and desired_goal
The achieved goal is the object's 7-element joint position and quaternion
The observation and both goal spaces are unbounded Box spaces
A reset restores the initial simulator state, randomises the object's orientation and runs 10 zero-action simulation steps
RobotEnv.reset samples a new goal and returns the observation
The default goal position ranges are x 0.96-1.04, y 0.81-0.89 (hand 1) or 0.60-0.68 (hand 2) and z 0.20-0.26
The target rotation is a uniformly random axis-angle with angle in [-pi, pi] and axis components in [-1, 1]
The EggHandOver default success thresholds are 0.01 m for position and 0.1 rad for rotation
The dense reward is exp(-(dist_multiplier*d_pos + d_rot)); the sparse reward is success - 1.0
The default dist_multiplier is 20.0
The simulator timestep is 0.002 s
n_substeps defaults to 20 simulation steps per call to step
dt is the model timestep times the number of substeps
The seed is drawn with gym.utils.seeding.np_random

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's Python random generator and the kinematics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake and the upstream MuJoCo model do not share a random stream

gaps: kinematic/analytic stand-in: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model; the action moves hand joint positions directly and the object is held fixed
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
the fake was never compared with the upstream MuJoCo environment (mujoco_py and gym 0.15.3 were not installed where the gate ran); trajectories and rewards differ

the upstream environment is the legacy Gym API (reset returns only the observation and step returns a 4-tuple); the fake returns the Gymnasium 5-tuple and applies the registered 75-step truncation itself
the observation is a plain Python list of both hands' joint positions and velocities plus the object's qpos and qvel; upstream returns float32 numpy arrays
goal sampling and the initial object rotation use Python's random.Random; upstream uses gym's numpy generator
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
